anchor.exact: The most telling feature of Common Ainu is the collapse of the palatalized consonant series (with merging of ^(✶)s^(y) and ^(✶)s after ^(✶)i)

statement.en: In Common Ainu, the palatalized consonant series collapsed, with *sʸ and *s merging after *i.
statement.ja: 共通アイヌ語において口蓋化子音系列は崩壊し、*i の後で *sʸ と *s が合流した。

entailment.quote: the collapse of the palatalized consonant series (with merging of ^(✶)s^(y) and ^(✶)s after ^(✶)i)

anchor.exact: the merger of the hypothetical lateral ^(✶)l with the flap ^(✶)ɾ

statement.en: In Common Ainu, the hypothetical lateral *l merged with the flap *ɾ.
statement.ja: 共通アイヌ語において、仮定された側音 *l は弾き音 *ɾ と合流した。

entailment.quote: the merger of the hypothetical lateral ^(✶)l with the flap ^(✶)ɾ

anchor.exact: (only at a later stage will the retroflex sound ^(✶)/ʈ ~ ɽ ~ ʈɽ/ merged with it too, cf. Nairo t- < ^(✶)l & ^(✶)ʈ, but r < ^(✶)ɾ)

statement.en: In Nairo Sakhalin Ainu, initial t- reflects Proto-Ainu *l and *ʈ, whereas r- reflects *ɾ.
statement.ja: 樺太アイヌ語内路方言において、語頭の t- は祖アイヌ語の *l および *ʈ を反映し、r- は *ɾ を反映する。

entailment.quote: Nairo t- < ^(✶)l & ^(✶)ʈ, but r < ^(✶)ɾ

anchor.exact: most likely, the replacement of the original trochaic foot by the iambic dominating in historical lects

statement.en: In Common Ainu, the original trochaic foot was most likely replaced by the iambic foot that dominates in historical lects.
statement.ja: 共通アイヌ語において、元々の強弱（トロカイオス）音脚は、歴史諸方言で支配的な弱強（ジャンボス）音脚に置換された可能性が高い。

entailment.quote: most likely, the replacement of the original trochaic foot by the iambic dominating in historical lects

anchor.exact: PA | ^(✶)/ti-ʔe-p/ ‘fish’, | Proto-Slavic | ^(✶)/genā/ | | | | lit. ‘the thing eaten (by everyone)’ {RES-eat-NML}

statement.en: The modern word for 'fish' (Saru cep, Horobetsu ciʔep, Raiciska ceh) reconstructs to Pre-Proto-Ainu *ti=(ʔ)e pe, literally 'the thing eaten (by everyone)'.
statement.ja: 「魚」を表す現代語形（沙流 cep、幌別 ciʔep、来知志 ceh）は、文字通りには「（皆によって）食べられるもの」を意味する前祖アイヌ語 *ti=(ʔ)e pe に再構される。

entailment.quote: Pre-PA | ^(✶)ti=(ʔ)e pe
entailment.note: The passage shows the reconstruction but does not mention the specific modern dialect forms listed in the statement.

anchor.exact: In this stage, the affiliative marker is still CVCVx (where “x” is an undetermined consonant)

statement.en: In Pre-Proto-Ainu, the affiliative marker had the phonological shape CVCVx, where x represents an undetermined consonant.
statement.ja: 前祖アイヌ語において、所属形接辞は CVCVx（x は未定の子音）という音韻形態を有していた。

entailment.quote: the affiliative marker is still CVCVx (where “x” is an undetermined consonant)

anchor.exact: classifiers (if any) were a productive and distinct feature of the language.

statement.en: In Pre-Proto-Ainu, numeral classifiers, if they existed, were a productive and distinct feature of the language.
statement.ja: 前祖アイヌ語において、助数詞（存在したとすれば）は生産的で明確な言語特徴であった。

entailment.quote: classifiers (if any) were a productive and distinct feature of the language.

anchor.exact: In Sakhalin Ainu, 〈h〉 represents /x/ (i.e., [ax], [iɕ], [uf], etc.).

statement.en: In Sakhalin Ainu phonological description, 〈h〉 represents the phoneme /x/, realized phonetically as [ax], [iɕ], [uf], and similar rhymes.
statement.ja: 樺太アイヌ語の記述において、〈h〉 は音素 /x/ を表し、音声的には [ax], [iɕ], [uf] などとして実現する。

entailment.quote: In Sakhalin Ainu, 〈h〉 represents /x/ (i.e., [ax], [iɕ], [uf], etc.)

anchor.exact: All Ainu dialects, with no exception, have five vocalic phonemes: /a e i o u/

statement.en: All Ainu dialects without exception possess five vocalic phonemes: /a/, /e/, /i/, /o/, and /u/.
statement.ja: 例外なくすべてのアイヌ語方言は、/a/、/e/、/i/、/o/、/u/の5母音音素をもつ。

entailment.quote: All Ainu dialects, with no exception, have five vocalic phonemes: /a e i o u/

anchor.exact: with allophonic vowel length in SA [a: e: i: o: u:] on stressed syllables.

statement.en: Sakhalin Ainu exhibits allophonic vowel length [a: e: i: o: u:] on stressed syllables.
statement.ja: 樺太アイヌ語では強勢音節において異音的な母音の長短[a: e: i: o: u:]が現れる。

entailment.quote: with allophonic vowel length in SA [a: e: i: o: u:] on stressed syllables

anchor.exact: Table 4 shows the phonological inventory of the Hokkaidō dialect of Saru (see, e.g., Tamura 2000: 17)

statement.en: The consonant inventory of Saru Ainu consists of /p/, /t/, /c/, /k/, /m/, /n/, /s/, /y/, /w/, /h/, /ɾ/, and phonetic glottal stop [ʔ].
statement.ja: 沙流アイヌ語の子音目録は /p/, /t/, /c/, /k/, /m/, /n/, /s/, /y/, /w/, /h/, /ɾ/ および音声的な声門閉鎖音 [ʔ] からなる。

anchor.exact: in the idiolect of Ginosuke Kikuchi, a speaker of the Bihoro dialect, the voiced retroflex plosive [ɖ] could be still heard by the time Hattori’s team collected data for the comparative dictionary of Ainu dialects

statement.en: In the Bihoro dialect idiolect of Ginosuke Kikuchi, the voiced retroflex plosive [ɖ] was attested.
statement.ja: 美幌方言の菊池銀之助の話者個人語において、有声そり舌破裂音[ɖ]が聞かれた。

conditions: in the idiolect of Ginosuke Kikuchi

entailment.quote: in the idiolect of Ginosuke Kikuchi, a speaker of the Bihoro dialect, the voiced retroflex plosive [ɖ] could be still heard

anchor.exact: Initial stressed syllables (< PHA high pitch accent) triggered the rising of a prothetic /h-/ in Bihoro words (Sidwell 1996: 180), whereas initial non-stressed syllables (< PHA low pitch accent) did not generate it.

statement.en: In Bihoro, initial syllables that had high pitch accent in Proto-Hokkaido Ainu developed a prothetic /h-/, while those with low pitch did not.
statement.ja: 美幌方言では、祖北海道アイヌ語で高ピッチアクセントを持っていた語頭音節に前置的/h-/が発生したが、低ピッチ音節には発生しなかった。

conditions: initial stressed syllables (< PHA high pitch accent)

entailment.quote: Initial stressed syllables (< PHA high pitch accent) triggered the rising of a prothetic /h-/ in Bihoro words, whereas initial non-stressed syllables (< PHA low pitch accent) did not generate it.

anchor.exact: These bear witness to the existence of the prothetic h- in Kuril Ainu dialects. Curiously enough, prothetic h- occurred along the loss of original h- for which there is no ready explanation as of yet.

statement.en: Early sources of Kuril Ainu attest both prothetic h- and the loss of original h-.
statement.ja: 千島アイヌ語の初期資料は前置的h-の存在と本来のh-の消失の双方を証拠づけている。

entailment.quote: These bear witness to the existence of the prothetic h- in Kuril Ainu dialects. Curiously enough, prothetic h- occurred along the loss of original h-

anchor.exact: SA and KA have noun and verb bases (= stems) distinguishing short and long vowels: /a aa e ee i ii o oo u uu/. Long vowels only appear in open syllables, otherwise the vowel is short.

statement.en: In Sakhalin and Kuril Ainu, noun and verb bases distinguish short and long vowels, with long vowels appearing only in open syllables.
statement.ja: 樺太アイヌ語および千島アイヌ語において、名詞語幹および動詞語幹は短母音と長母音を区別し、長母音は開音節にのみ現れる。

entailment.quote: SA and KA have noun and verb bases (= stems) distinguishing short and long vowels: /a aa e ee i ii o oo u uu/. Long vowels only appear in open syllables

anchor.exact: SA & KA long vowel corresponds to high pitch in HA. This was acknowledged for the first time by Hattori (1967).

statement.en: Long vowels in Sakhalin and Kuril Ainu regularly correspond to high pitch in Hokkaido Ainu.
statement.ja: 樺太アイヌ語および千島アイヌ語の長母音は、北海道アイヌ語の高ピッチに規則的に対応する。

entailment.quote: SA & KA long vowel corresponds to high pitch in HA.

anchor.exact: SA (and apparently KA) vowel length is clearly phonetic: long vowels occur in the stem if this is an open syllable. Vowels not belonging to the stem are always short

statement.en: In Sakhalin Ainu, vowel length is phonetic rather than phonemic, occurring in open stem syllables while vowels outside the stem are always short.
statement.ja: 樺太アイヌ語における母音長は音素的ではなく音声的なものであり、開音節の語幹に生じ、語幹外の母音は常に短い。

entailment.quote: SA (and apparently KA) vowel length is clearly phonetic: long vowels occur in the stem if this is an open syllable. Vowels not belonging to the stem are always short

anchor.exact: Hokkaidō Ainu gave up vowel length, and pitch accent become phonemic (as in nína ‘collect firewood’ vs. niná ‘crush’, etc.).

statement.en: Hokkaido Ainu lost vowel length, and pitch accent became phonemic, as in minimal pairs like nína 'collect firewood' versus niná 'crush'.
statement.ja: 北海道アイヌ語は母音長を失い、nína「薪を拾う」対 niná「すり潰す」のような最小対においてピッチアクセントが音素化した。

entailment.quote: Hokkaidō Ainu gave up vowel length, and pitch accent become phonemic (as in nína ‘collect firewood’ vs. niná ‘crush’, etc.)

anchor.exact: debuccalization (Fallon 2002: 123–202) that takes place in Sakhalin Ainu, whereby the original place of articulation of the Proto-Ainu consonants ^(✶)/p t k/ moves to the glottis when in final position

statement.en: In Sakhalin Ainu, Proto-Ainu final consonants */p/, */t/, and */k/ underwent debuccalization, moving their place of articulation to the glottis.
statement.ja: 樺太アイヌ語において、祖アイヌ語の末子音*/p/、*/t/、*/k/は調音点が声門へと移動する声門音化（口腔音消失）を起こした。

entailment.quote: the original place of articulation of the Proto-Ainu consonants ^(✶)/p t k/ moves to the glottis when in final position

anchor.exact: from ^(✶)sih via regular h > s after /i/, cf. the affiliative (aff) form ^(✶)sik-i(hi) ‘one’s eye’ > SA sik-ihi

statement.en: In Sakhalin Ainu, /h/ regularly changes to /s/ following /i/.
statement.ja: 樺太アイヌ語において、/h/は/i/の直後で規則的に/s/へと変化する。

entailment.quote: regular h > s after /i/

anchor.exact: This change also affects the flap /ɾ/ after intermediary assimilation

statement.en: In Sakhalin Ainu, the flap /r/ before a consonant also debuccalized to /h/ via an intermediate stage of total assimilation ([-r-C-] > [-C-C-] > [-hC-]).
statement.ja: 樺太アイヌ語において、子音に先行する弾き音/r/も中間段階の完全同化（[-r-C-] > [-C-C-] > [-hC-]）を経て声門音化を起こし/h/となった。

entailment.quote: This change also affects the flap /ɾ/ after intermediary assimilation: [-ɾ‿C-] > [-C‿C-] > [-hC-]

anchor.exact: Standard Japanese tsukegi ‘matches’ → Saru Ainu cikenki id., SJ azuki ‘sweet beans’ → Saru Ainu antuki

statement.en: Loanwords from Northern (Tōhoku) Japanese into Saru Ainu preserve prenasalized consonants, as seen in cikenki 'matches' (from Standard Japanese tsukegi) and antuki 'sweet beans' (from Standard Japanese azuki).
statement.ja: 東北日本語方言から沙流アイヌ語への借用語には、共通語のtsukegiに対するcikenki「マッチ」や、azukiに対するantuki「小豆」のように前鼻音化子音が保持されている。

entailment.quote: e.g., Standard Japanese tsukegi ‘matches’ → Saru Ainu cikenki id., SJ azuki ‘sweet beans’ → Saru Ainu antuki
entailment.note: Passage gives examples but does not explicitly state that both show prenasalized consonant retention; only antuki likely does.

anchor.exact: Proto-Ainu is the hypothetical parent language from which all documented lects have historically formed during the course of approximately a thousand years

statement.en: Proto-Ainu is reconstructed as having diversified into all documented lects over a time depth of approximately one thousand years.
statement.ja: 祖アイヌ語は、記録されたすべての諸変種へと歴史的におよそ1000年の時間深度をかけて分化した母言語である。

entailment.quote: Proto-Ainu is the hypothetical parent language from which all documented lects have historically formed during the course of approximately a thousand years

anchor.exact: Pan-Ainu a (sg.) / rok (pl.) ‘to sit down’ > durative or perfective

statement.en: The Pan-Ainu singular verb a and plural verb rok 'to sit down' grammaticalized into durative or perfective markers.
statement.ja: 汎アイヌ語の動詞 a（単数）および rok（複数）「座る」は、継続または完了の標識へと文法化した。

entailment.quote: Pan-Ainu a (sg.) / rok (pl.) ‘to sit down’ > durative or perfective

anchor.exact: ani ‘to hold’ > ‘with; by’ instrumental

statement.en: The verb ani 'to hold' grammaticalized into the instrumental marker 'with; by'.
statement.ja: 動詞 ani「持つ」は具格標識「〜で、〜によって」へと文法化した。

entailment.quote: ani ‘to hold’ > ‘with; by’ instrumental

anchor.exact: kusu ‘reason’ > ‘because; due to’

statement.en: The noun kusu 'reason' grammaticalized into the causal conjunction 'because; due to'.
statement.ja: 名詞 kusu「理由」は「〜だから、〜のために」を意味する接続詞へと文法化した。

entailment.quote: kusu ‘reason’ > ‘because; due to’

anchor.exact: ne anaphoric pronoun > ne copula

statement.en: The copula ne grammaticalized from the anaphoric pronoun ne.
statement.ja: コピュラ ne は前方照応代名詞 ne から文法化した。

entailment.quote: ne anaphoric pronoun > ne copula

statement.ja: 欠如動詞を派生する接尾辞 -sak ~ -nak は、動詞 sak「欠く」から文法化した。

anchor.exact: Ainu numbers may appear along with two suffixes: things VΟ-p ~ CΟ-pe (from pe ‘thing’) and human beings VΟ-n ~ CΟ-iw (from aynu ‘human being’)

statement.en: Ainu numerals may occur with two suffixes: -p ~ -pe for things (from pe 'thing') and -n ~ -iw for human beings (from aynu 'human being').
statement.ja: アイヌ語の数詞は、事物を表す接尾辞 -p ~ -pe（pe「もの」に由来）および人間を表す接尾辞 -n ~ -iw（aynu「人間」に由来）の2つの接尾辞を伴って現れ得る。

entailment.quote: Ainu numbers may appear along with two suffixes: things VΟ-p ~ CΟ-pe (from pe ‘thing’) and human beings VΟ-n ~ CΟ-iw (from aynu ‘human being’)

anchor.exact: two word-classifiers: to for ‘X days’ and suy for ‘X times’.

statement.en: Ainu possesses two word-classifiers used with numbers: to for counting days and suy for counting times.
statement.ja: アイヌ語には数詞とともに用いられる2つの語助数詞、すなわち日数を数える to と回数を数える suy がある。

entailment.quote: two word-classifiers: to for ‘X days’ and suy for ‘X times’
